Lecture 1 — Geometry as the Study of Smooth Change

A philosophical and geometric introduction to differential geometry.
Curves vs surfaces vs manifolds.
The idea of studying shape through derivatives.

Lecture 2 — Smooth Curves: Parametrization, Arc Length, and Reparametrization

Smooth curves, regularity, arc-length parameter, geometric meaning of velocity and acceleration.

Lecture 3 — Curvature of Curves: The Frenet Frame

Tangent, normal, binormal, curvature, torsion.
Frenet–Serret formulas with geometric intuition.

Helices, geodesics on cylinders, classical examples of curves studied by Gauss.

Smooth surfaces, patch parametrizations, tangent plane, normal vector, and implicit surfaces.

Metric induced by the ambient space.

Lecture 7 — The Second Fundamental Form and Classical Curvatures

Normal curvature, principal curvatures, Gaussian curvature, mean curvature.
Geometric meaning and examples.

Lecture 8 — The Gauss Map and Gauss’ Theorema Egregium

The deep result that curvature is intrinsic.
How bending without stretching preserves Gaussian curvature.

Lecture 9 — Geodesics: The Straightest Possible Paths

Derivation of geodesic equations, Christoffel symbols, examples on sphere, plane, cylinder.

Lecture 10 — Differential Forms and Exterior Calculus (Conceptual Introduction)

Orientation, differential 1-forms, wedge product, integration on curves and surfaces.

Lecture 11 — Tensors and Tensor Fields on Manifolds

Multilinear algebra, covariant vs contravariant indices, type-

(r,s) tensors, coordinate transformations, metric tensor.

Lecture 12 — Connections and Covariant Derivatives

Directional derivatives on manifolds.
Levi-Civita connection.
Covariant differentiation of vector fields.
Parallel transport.

Lecture 13 — Curvature Revisited: Riemann Curvature Tensor

The full curvature tensor, sectional curvature, Ricci curvature, scalar curvature.
Geometric meaning, symmetries, and intuition.

Lecture 14 — Riemannian Manifolds and Geometric Structures

Riemannian metric, length of curves, completeness, Hopf–Rinow theorem (conceptual).

Lecture 15 — Lie Groups and Symmetry in Differential Geometry

Basic introduction to Lie groups as smooth manifolds with multiplication.
Examples: sphere, orthogonal group, Euclidean motions.

Lecture 16 — Modern View: The Geometry of Space(-Time)

Applications in relativity:
Lorentzian manifolds, metric signature, geodesics as physical trajectories.
Differential geometry as the language of physics.
